extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, data analysts, and journalists using or reproducing Pew Research Center's State of the News Media fact sheets
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and selection rules Pew Research Center used to compile the State of the News Media fact sheets, including data sourcing, vetting, entity selection, audience metric calculation, and digital outreach/audit procedures for TV, newspapers and digital news outlets. Useful for researchers reproducing or evaluating these fact sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of third‑party industry data (aggregation and licensing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State of the News Media fact sheets consist of data originally generated by other individuals or organizations that Pew Research Center then collected and aggregated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center researchers first tried to determine what data had been collected for the media sectors studied and by whom. In many cases this included securing rights to data through licensing fees or other means, and often included paying for use of the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data vetting and validity assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers studied the data closely to determine where elements reinforced each other and where there were apparent contradictions or gaps, and endeavored to determine the value and validity of each dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This often involved going back to the sources that collected the data in the first place. Where there were conflicts, the Center included all relevant sources and tried to explain their differences, either in chart notes or in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full citation and explanation of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: All sources are cited in chart and graphic notes or within the text of the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some data providers may update data for past and future years on an annual basis; when conflicts or differences exist, researchers explain differences in chart notes/text so readers can see provenance and updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comscore TV audience data usage and comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Pew Research Center uses Comscore StationView Essentials® and TV Essentials® for TV news audience analysis (data included from 2016 onward); local TV from StationView Essentials®, cable and network from TV Essentials®.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier versions of the TV fact sheets used Nielsen Media Research (data stretching back to 2007). Because of differences between the two sets of data points, figures from prior years are not directly comparable with the Comscore data shown here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comscore digital audience data: entity selection and vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Comscore entry representing an outlet or website ('entity') was individually vetted by researchers; unusual shifts in data over time were checked with Comscore analysts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities that registered increases or declines in unique visitors over the time period studied that were likely due to inorganic changes in measurement or site structure were considered to not have data that could be trended and were removed from the analysis. Researchers consulted Comscore analysts throughout the entity selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for total‑domain entities; use of custom entities when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: For all outlets, entities that are representative of an entire web domain ('total domain entities') were used whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When domain entities were incomplete (i.e., they did not represent traffic to an entire web domain), custom entities that represent the total domain were used when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple/comparable Comscore entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple entities of the same URL that were the result of a structure change in the Comscore database over time were considered comparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers treated such multiple entries as comparable for trend purposes, subject to vetting and consultation with Comscore analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of entities with inorganic measurement or site‑structure changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities with increases or declines in unique visitors likely due to inorganic changes in measurement or site structure were removed from trend analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such entities were considered to not have data that could be trended; researchers checked unusual shifts with Comscore analysts before removing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper selection (top 50 by circulation and Comscore matching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers assembled a list of the top 49 newspapers by average Sunday circulation (various years per dataset) then added The Wall Street Journal to produce a top 50 list; each was matched with its associated total‑domain entities in Comscore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers analyzed Comscore data for October, November and December in each year. The methodology documents the specific 50 entities used in each year cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: News outlet inclusion criteria (selection from Comscore categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers assessed all domains from 11 Comscore categories with at least 10 million average monthly unique digital visitors in Q4 2022 and then selected news outlets using defined criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be included an outlet must be a publisher of original content about news (current events affecting public life), judged by homepage material. Evidence of original reporting (interviews, eyewitness accounts, referral to source documents) by a dedicated reporter/editorial staff was required, or the site could self‑describe as producing news via navigation/about/advertising language. Exclusions: sites focused entirely on reviews/advice/recipes/unedited raw data; primarily user‑generated or aggregated content platforms (e.g., Medium, Reddit, Wikipedia); and branded content sites (e.g., NBA.com).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience metrics and time window for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Minutes per visit and unique visitors for October to December of each year come from the Comscore Media Metrix® Multi‑Platform U.S. database for Total Digital Population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons year‑over‑year are between monthly averages of October to December data in each year. For sites that didn’t meet the reporting threshold for one month out of a quarter, researchers averaged the two months for which data was available.

rubrics_metrics.name: News outlet digital audit procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers studied outreach avenues outlets could take to engage audiences: mobile apps, newsletters, Apple News, Flipboard, podcasts, comments and social media presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mobile apps, researchers searched Google Play and iOS App Store for official apps. For newsletters, they searched the outlet’s site for a sign‑up form. For Apple News and Flipboard they searched respective apps/websites for official channels/pages. For podcasts they searched iTunes and each outlet’s site. An outlet was determined to support comments if at least one of the first five stories on its homepage supported comments at the time of analysis. For social media outreach, researchers searched for official pages/accounts/channels on each platform and on the outlet’s primary website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital economic data source and comparability caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Economics data for the digital fact sheet comes from eMarketer’s U.S. Ad Spending estimates; data from previous years is updated annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eMarketer adjusted its format definitions in 2017 and 2018, substantially changing category structures; because of these changes, data from 2016 and earlier are not included in the current report and should be sought in archived versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting included entities and year‑by‑year cohorts
rubrics_metrics.description: The methodology documents the exact lists of entities (domains/sites) used in each year’s cohort for transparency and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report provides year‑by‑year lists for newspapers and news outlets (e.g., 50 newspapers per year, 105 news outlets for 2022) so readers can see which specific domains were analyzed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about funding and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The methodology discloses Pew Research Center's funding sources and staff contributions to the fact sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pew Research Center acknowledges primary funder (The Pew Charitable Trusts), additional supporters (e.g., Knight Foundation), and lists staff and contributors involved in data analysis, web production, copy editing and communications.
